name: power
title: Battery & Power
description: Battery level and time left, and with the optional power watcher everything about where the power goes: the draw over the last hours, what uses power now and why, and what used the battery today, this week and ever, in watt-hours.
author: pal

settings.label: Power watcher state
settings.description: Optional state.json written by the `power` watcher. It adds measured draw, warnings and top consumers; a stale file is ignored.

store.tagline: Battery level, and exactly what is draining it
features: The level, where the power comes from and the time left, from macOS `pmset` or Linux `upower`, in one plain sentence (`Drawing 12 W · 1 h 48 min left`, `Charging at 38 W · full in 40 min`)
With the `power` watcher: six hours of draw as a chart, the stretches on the charger shaded and the charge level dashed over it, and today's watt-hours as a share of a full charge
Now: the watcher's warning in words, the draw split between the apps and chip and the screen and the rest, and the processes using power with their watts and why (CPU, wakeups, disk, network)
Today, 7 days and All time: what used the battery in watt-hours with each one's share, the screen and short-lived processes named plainly; a window spent on the charger ranks by activity instead
Battery health, cycle count and temperature as tiles; Enter finds the process in Processes, cmd+C copies its name

The bar stays quiet while healthy by default and returns for a low battery, a warning or a heavy draw; hover shows the popover (the level, the last hour, the warning, the top four), a click opens the palette

battery.title: Battery
battery.description: Battery level, and the time left once that is the question being asked. Hidden while healthy by its rules: on battery from 50%, on the charger from 20%, unless the power watcher warns or measures a draw of 15 W. Amber at 20%, red at 10% or on a critical warning. Hover shows the popover (the level, the last hour's draw, the warning, what uses power now, today's watt-hours); a click opens the Battery & Power palette.
